guards.name: evidence-receipt
guards.invariant: A terminal run's receipt is strict at every level and carries the graph/config/input fingerprints, a source and observation instant for every fact, a filed binding proof for every verified write, and one explicit confidence; `verified-done` is refused for non-verified confidence, an unresolved mandatory fact or obligation, any warning, or a failure id, each proven by a violating fixture. Redaction is DECLARED: every leaf of every registered canonical-input sample and every used contract's sealed example carries a classification whose transform its classification permits, an undeclared leaf fails loud rather than dropping, a declaration that disagrees with domain/secrets.ts fails. retains complete supplied values with their original classifications; positive gate/value/declaration proofs replace classification-based masking expectations. Malformed classification/transform/scope declarations and unknown keys refuse, and receipts do not invent unsupplied canary values. The diagnostic-bundle half of ref guards-and-tests activates with the bundle capture slice. — a receipt is bound to the surfaces its derivation CONSUMES, never to the descriptor's source closure: `descriptorFingerprint` is the closure the RUN executed under, read from its own envelope, so a settled receipt re-derives byte-identically after any edit that leaves every consumed surface intact, and a receipt that took the current build's `contractFingerprint` stranded every already-settled run on the next unrelated edit. Resolvability is a named check table — `workflow-identity`, `descriptor-version`, `canonical-input`, `evidence-graph`, `terminal-dependency-set`, `declared-evidence` — printed in full with both fingerprints, `[held]`/`[MOVED]`/`[skip]` distinct and no waiver arm. `declared-evidence` is the one check whose baseline is the stored receipt row, because the declared redaction and obligation tables live OUTSIDE every descriptor closure and can move with `contractFingerprint` byte-identical; the immutable insert stays underneath as the backstop. — a GATE's durable evidence is a `gate_results` row and never a checkpoint, so a resolved gate node emits its payload's leaves as facts sourced `gate-result` (carrying authority's own `resolvedBy`/`resolvedAt`, never a payload claim), ONE `kind: "gate"` decision naming the approver, the instant, the resolving command and the bound evidence digest, and a `verified` obligation in place of the `unknown` a checkpoint-only derivation reported. The outcome is DECLARED per `(workflow, gate)` in `src/domain/trust/gate-decisions.ts` and never sniffed from a field name: every gate node of every registered descriptor has a declaration whose decision and bound-evidence leaves classify under a `gate-result` redaction scope, an undeclared gate and an unlisted arm value both fail loud, an orphan declaration or gate-scoped classification fails, and a foreign run's gate row, a gate that left the graph and an undeclared arm are executed as negative controls against the REAL gated descriptor, and the UNDECLARED `(workflow, gate)` pair — unreachable through the builder precisely because every registered gate node is declared — is pinned directly on `gateDecisionFor`, which is the only route from a stored row to a `DecisionEvidence.outcome`. — an orphan task-output classification is judged against the BUILD MANIFEST task set rather than only the descriptor-reachable one, because observed-log emission redacts by declaration for every task the executor runs and a composed fixture descriptor must borrow a manifest-known id. C updates only the unsettled/interrupted negative fixture to omit settled completion evidence; the original named refusal assertions and frozen receipt/redaction controls remain. Complete local values are verified separately through retainLocalEvidenceValue and RedactedFieldSchema for every classification, with original classification and nested values preserved.

guards.name: identity-gate-before-commit

The terminal arm landed with separations chunk 3 because a read-only chunk produces an APPROVED SUBJECT a later composition binds a write's expected side to, so a terminal result reachable without the gate hands that composition an unconfirmed identity. The registered gate is additionally pinned to ref write-safety's IdentityApprovalResult schema hash — the exact value executeResolveGate compares an incoming payload against — so §14.6 risk 5 (a gate result becoming free-form control state) is structurally closed. guards.name: multi-worker-overlap
guards.invariant: ACTIVATED BY (ref execution-and-sessions rows C1-C4). More than one REAL `runWorkerLoop` instance, with distinct worker ids, races ONE workflow queue over ONE shared authority database, and the durable claim set is sampled at every span event and every driver call rather than read once at the end. Two facts hold at once and pull in opposite directions: no worker EVER owns two rows in `claimed|validating|running` (ref execution-and-sessions, sampled live so a double claim released before the end could not hide), and the fleet genuinely overlaps -- the observed maximum of workers holding work simultaneously equals the worker count, which is ref execution-and-sessions's 'parallelism silently serializes' risk stated as a measurement. Every enqueued run is executed exactly once, claimed by exactly one worker, and ends terminal `done` at claim generation 1 and attempt 1, so a second claim or a requeue is visible in authority rather than only in a report. A row held by a live loop is never served to a sibling `claimNext` and the holder's own second `claimNext` throws by name. Wall-clock delay never takes a live claim. Explicit recovery fails only the selected interrupted run while a sibling heartbeat preserves its owner, generation and attempt; the failed run is never re-claimed. After an explicit claim-fenced reassignment, the prior owner reports `lost` and abandons instead of stamping a heartbeat over the new owner.

guards.name: notification-durability
guards.invariant: (ref dashboard-surfaces §2.6/§10.4 b; ref operator-trust): a notification is a durable record FIRST and a desktop delivery second. `publish` settles create-or-fold in one authority transaction and only then attempts OS delivery, and the load-bearing arm injects a delivery that throws — the item must still be durably unread with its count and version untouched, because the operator who missed the toast has only the inbox left. Each of ref dashboard-surfaces §2.6's closed triggers commits an item and routes to its ratified b channel (failed/gate-waiting/write-parked/repeating/storage → ping, verified-done → inbox), each carries its own dedupe identity that excludes the occurrence, and a repeat FOLDS into the one (actorId, dedupeFingerprint) row — count up, lastSeenAt advanced, unread again — rather than minting a second. Snooze suppresses delivery only and never flips status; read state and snooze move independently; a stale version is refused. The trigger event union is ids, closed codes, and counts, so notification text has no free-text channel a captured value could enter through.

guards.invariant: Ref execution-and-sessions (): no login path reaches the UCSD SSO form or the Duo WebAuthn assertion without presenting a DuoCeremonyLeaseToken, and one credential admits one Duo ceremony at a time. The token is minted and retired ONLY by the lease store (src/infra/sqlite/authority-database.ts, through src/base/duo-ceremony-lease.ts's module-private WeakSets); the brand is conjured by `as`/`satisfies` nowhere outside that module; defineVerifiedLoginRecipe (src/backend/systems/browser-shared/authenticated-application.ts) is the ONE caller of the gate's withCeremony; every store login recipe is the wrapper's {navigate, ceremony} shape rather than a single flow, and every SSO-helper call in a store presents `token`. Duo's signature counter is per CREDENTIAL while Duo Autopilot's copy is per browser PROFILE, so two ceremonies in one second present the same floored counter and Duo reads the non-advancing one as a cloned key — which BURNS the profile (). Each arm runs against tests/architecture/fixtures/duo-lease-recipe-violation.ts, the exact pre-lease recipe shape, so a walker that resolved nothing cannot report the tree clean. Minting diagnostics name the current SQLite authority owner; lease forgery and structural lifetime controls remain enforced. Owner closure minting is restricted to the actual session manager; lifecycle effect minting is restricted to the process supervisor to prevent forged exit or birth proof. A durable stop receipt is accepted after an early OS exit only for the unchanged supervisor record, member and born child; replacement, uncertain ownership and closed supervision refuse without signaling or granting resource closure.

guards.name: step-omission-invariants
guards.invariant: an operator may omit a timeline step at start and type the facts it would have read; only a step folder's own declared `omission` may say what a TASK node of that step would have produced, gates and transactions are never substituted, and ALWAYS-GATE () is a planner invariant, not a per-descriptor promise. The production registry declares three omissions, all on `separations` — `kronos-timecard`, `ucpath-transaction` and `kuali-finalization`, each authored in its own step folder's `omission.ts` and carried onto the descriptor by that folder's `nodes.category(..., { omission })` — and every sweep here pins those three BY NAME plus the one in-test fixture declaration, asserting at the end that it visited EXACTLY that set, so a deleted, renamed or unwired production declaration turns the sweep red instead of quietly shrinking it. The fixture (a read, the `identity-approval` operator gate, a post-gate task and a transaction, across `reading`/`identity-check`/`writing`) exists only for the arms the registry cannot reach: the definition-time refusals, which no registered descriptor may contain and still import, and the `blocked` cascade arm Separations has no instance of. (a) `defineWorkflowDescriptor` throws at DEFINITION TIME when an omission's `produces` names a gate or a transaction node of its own step — proved for both kinds, and separately for a form that declares a duplicate field key; (b) every production omittable step's `stepOmissionCascade` row equals its exact pinned row (Separations: three `{ state: "omittable", forces: [] }` rows), while the fixture keeps the `omittable`-or-`blocked` union assertion, since letting the real cascade run un-caught is what proves it never throws for any refusal but `dependency-omitted`; (c) every RAW step-folder declaration (`KRONOS_TIMECARD_OMISSION` and its two siblings, imported from the `omission.ts` modules themselves rather than read back off an already-parsed `spec.form`) parses through `StepOmissionFormSchema` with the exact pinned field keys, no duplicate key and exactly the pinned `produces` node ids, and the registry is reconciled against that pinned set in BOTH directions, so a folder that stops wiring its declaration through `nodes.category` is red too; (d) `planStepOmissions`, driven with the cascade's own exported placeholder facts (`stepOmissionPlaceholderFacts`), never classifies ANY gate node as `asserted` or `omitted` in three plan shapes per declaration — the step alone, the step together with its cascade `forces` set, and every omittable step of the descriptor at once — with Separations' `identity-approval` gate required to be present and to EXECUTE (classified neither way, under a refusal-free plan) in all three, and each production plan's node classification pinned: `dates` and `receipt` are the only asserted nodes, while `timecard-search`, `timecard`, `clear-pending`, `file-termination` and `finalize-kuali` are only ever omitted. There is no separate "no separations omission produces identity-approval" arm: a declaration naming the gate throws at import, so that assertion could not fail; the invariant lives in (c)'s exact `produces` pinning and (d)'s planner sweep.

guards.name: worker-loop-writes-only-through-the-service
guards.invariant: worker loop, executor, sequencer, compositions, recovery sweep and positive continuations cannot call or extract lifecycle repository mutators. Type-resolved scan includes the backend runtime and Runs helpers, with only Task-4 command/fan-out and negative-resolution paths excluded. Negative controls detect direct, aliased and relocated writes; worker capability preserves its five existing operations and adds only authenticated delegation admission; command-family transition remains excluded.

guards.name: rerun-prefill-boundary
guards.invariant: Descriptor schema, source version and copied-value coordinates are checked before a new source-bound plan can become work. The retired checkpoint-save command has no active or deferred arm; provenance never grants replay authority.

guards.name: composition-reads-no-environment-leaf
guards.invariant: Config modules never read process.env. Hostile unrelated noise cannot change config or provenance. Every cataloged refused key blocks dashboard, worker and dry-run composition before value reads or authority, browser or spawn effects. The canonical credential reader is the only config scan exclusion; neighboring environment readers and aliased or computed resolver access remain forbidden.

guards.name: workflow-operation-display-boundary
guards.invariant: 's in-process operation-display vocabulary retains a browser-safe runtime import closure, with no Node builtin, browser runtime or store/driver implementation reach. Only compiler-produced complete displays freeze into recursively strict serializable snapshots; the real reader validates envelope identity and content digest, refuses missing complete structure, nested unknown keys and executable values, and never substitutes a current descriptor. Legacy capability remains active for definitions without complete declarations. Positive compiler/freeze/read round-trip and Node/store, forged projection, nested unknown/function, wrong identity, missing snapshot and changed payload/digest negative controls prove both boundaries.

guards.name: test-artifact-ownership
guards.invariant: Generated test-results, coverage and parity scratch remain ignored and untracked; the existing owned test runner keeps scratch outside the checkout and accepted evidence has an external owner. The pure injected-listing policy test supplies tracked-output, missing-ignore and in-checkout negative controls.

guards.name: sqlite-authority-boundary
guards.invariant: The public SQLite entrypoint never exposes a raw database connection or SQL escape hatch, and only the reviewed private adapters import node:sqlite. The test reads current source and checks a typed adapter boundary. The private adapter inventory is exact and order independent. Public parameters, returns, fields, getters, aliases and nested generic values cannot expose SQLite handles; private local use returning a closed scalar is allowed. Recursive type traversal examines generic payloads before cycle and library prototype cuts. log; direct, alias, nested, Promise/Map, cyclic and cast escape controls pass.

guards.name: start-plan-contract
guards.invariant: The browser and server share one strict start-plan wire contract. The mixed schema/type/source test checks defaults, refusals and declaration ownership intact under architecture.

guards.name: synthetic-database-admission-boundary
guards.invariant: Synthetic database fixtures use the real AuthorityDatabase and RuntimeAdmission through a narrow value-import closure. The helper, dashboard harness and shared launch-fixture closure cannot reach test-data readers, registry or CLI composition. Positive controls retain real authority/admission reach; broad imports and injected value reexports prove forbidden transitive reach is detected.

guards.name: native-doctor-limits
guards.invariant: Doctor refuses excess native event count, UTF-8 payload bytes and run identities before parsing, without changing authority bytes.

guards.name: readonly-authority-snapshot
guards.invariant: Authority inspection and backup readers include committed WAL through a private verified copy in a separate process, without source writes or releasing live SQLite process locks; unsafe companions and changed source identities or held copy descriptors refuse.

guards.name: admission-identity
guards.invariant: Reason: opaque profile registration exposed a dependency cycle and an unchecked issuer escape. Only the existing token-protected RuntimeAdmission constructor registers issued identities; consumers use the single identity owner, whose RuntimeAdmission dependency stays type-only; its only runtime dependency is the exact error catalog for the two shared refusal classes. Negative mutations reject unknown names and runtime dependencies as well as foreign, aliased, escaped, dynamic and nonconstructor registration. Credential-store, ChatGPT credential repository and restore-snapshot imports must erase the RuntimeAdmission dependency at declaration level; verbatim emit and mixed-specifier mutations protect against the observed erasure-head initialization cycle.

repositoryChecks.name: completed-restore-custody
repositoryChecks.invariant: Reason: settled restore suspects outlive their journal, and the raw public relocation lease bypasses the profile wrapper's unsupported-relocation check. Strict completed history binds exact profile/operation/file identities and complete companions before credential inventory. Raw relocation refuses nonempty history before destination or journal effects; unrelated registry mutations preserve it, and interrupted history publication settles once without accepting divergence.

repositoryChecks.name: public-repository-privacy
repositoryChecks.invariant: Private HR inputs and credentials must not enter the public tree. Inspect staged paths and textual blobs; allow only named synthetic documents and known synthetic tokens in reviewed example locations. Report paths and rules without values.
